passages.title: Ps. 142:1–2
passages.text: The words here express earnest prayer in the face of danger: **cry out**, **plead for mercy**, **pour out my complaint**, and **tell my trouble**. Each of these acts is directed toward the Lord.

passages.title: Ps. 142:3–4
passages.text: These verses express what people often feel when being threatened: out of energy, beset by dangers, confused, and painfully alone.

passages.title: Ps. 142:5–7
passages.text: The final section ties the whole psalm together. **Cry to you** echoes v. 1 , while **you are my refuge** echoes v. 4 ; and **I am brought very low** summarizes vv. 3–4 . This section enables the faithful to pray with boldness and with confidence in the Lord’s unflagging care.

notes.text: **Psalm** . This individual lament is a companion to Psalm 57 . It is also similar to Psalms 140–141 , with the faithful person praying for protection from persecutors.
